title: STAT 110 Final: Probability and Grouped Data

allowance.rules: Student confirmed one sheet, both sides, for exam use. Paper size and content restrictions are not supplied.

blocks.setup: Rows are commuter status; columns are cycling status. The question wording chooses the reference group (denominator).

steps.label: Counts
steps.text: Among 25 commuters, 10 cycle and 15 do not. Among 15 noncommuters, 5 cycle and 10 do not. Totals: 30 cycle; 25 do not.

steps.label: Commuters among cyclists
steps.text: 10 / 15 = 66.7% of cyclists. Reference group: cyclists. P(A|B) and P(B|A) usually differ because the reference groups differ.

steps.label: Row percentages
steps.text: Within the commuter row: 10/25 = 40.0% cycle; 15/25 = 60.0% do not. Divide each cell by its row total; each row sums to 100%.

steps.label: Column percentages
steps.text: Within the cycle column: 10/15 = 66.7% commuters; 5/15 = 33.3% noncommuters. Divide each cell by its column total; each column sums to 100%.

blocks.takeaway: Choose the group named after 'among' / 'of' first. Divide the overlap by that group's total; state the group in words. Assume equally weighted cases and a non-empty reference group.

blocks.text: Report proportions as percentages rounded to 1 decimal place and name the reference group: '40.0% of commuters.' (Outline reporting rule.)

Split cases by a categorical variable; calculate one summary (e.g., mean or count) per non-empty group. Output has one row per group, not per original case. Compare like with like: mean vs mean, total vs total.
